Brief facts necessary to appreciate the issue(s) in the present case, as noted in the Petition, are as follows: (f) The issue of there being a substantial conflict of interest, in case PTC is permitted to act as a member in the Petitioner exchange while also retaining its shareholding above 5%, was specifically raised by the Applicant and also the other Power Exchange in the proceedings in Petition No. 287/MP/2018. In this regard, the RoP dated 8.4.2021 in Petition No. 287/MP/2018 had a categorical statement recorded on behalf of HPX that the shareholding of PTC shall be brought down to 5% in terms of the PMR 2010 as and when it becomes a member of the Petitioner’s Power Exchange. The same contention was reiterated by HPX, as recorded in the Commission’s order dated 12.5.2021 in Petition No. 287/MP/2021. (g) It is also relevant to mention that the Petitioner has had more than four years since authorisation. In the background of the specific and unequivocal undertaking given on behalf of the Petitioner that the shareholding of PTC would be brought down 8. The matter was listed for hearing on 15.1.2026 and 3.3.2026. During the hearing on 3.3.2026, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, while reiterating the submissions made in the Petition, submitted that, in compliance with the Record of Proceedings dated 16.12.2025, the Petitioner has also filed its note of submissions dated 2.3.2026, indicating the reasons for seeking the period of three years to reduce its shareholding to 5%. 10. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioner strongly opposed the prayer of IEX for the impleadment and submitted that the matter being regulatory in nature did not need the intervention of a third party. The learned counsel also submitted that IEX had no locus standi in this case as it was not in any way an aggrieved person. 11. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission reserved the Petition as well as IA for order. 12. We have considered the submissions by the Petitioner and the Intervenor, IEX. The present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner seeking the grant of time to one of the promoter shareholders, namely PTC, to dilute its stake in the Petitioner Company to meet the requirements/ compliance under Regulation 15 of the PMR 2021. However, before dealing with the above aspect, it is necessary to first decide on the application filed by IEX, seeking impleadment as a party Respondent in the present Petition and permission to file its reply. without any application, and on such terms as may appear to it to be just, direct that any of the following persons may be added as a party: (a) any person who ought to have been joined as plaintiff or defendant, but not added; or (b) any person whose presence before the court may be necessary in order to enable the court to effectively and completely adjudicate upon and settle the question involved in the suit. This Commission is vested with a similar discretion by virtue of Regulation 37 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission ( _Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023_ . However, it is equally trite law that if a person is not found to be “a proper party” or “a necessary party”, the court does not have jurisdiction to order his impleadment against the wishes of a Plaintiff. A “necessary party” is a person who ought to have been joined as a party to the suit and in whose absence an effective decree cannot be passed by the court. Whereas a “proper party” is a person whose presence would enable the court to completely, effectively and properly adjudicate upon all the matters and issues, though he may not be a person in favour of or against whom a decree is to be made. As regards the ‘necessary party’, neither any relief has been prayed against IEX, nor is it the case that no effective order can be passed in the present case in the absence of IEX. Hence, IEX cannot be considered a necessary party. Similarly, we are unable to see how the presence of IEX is required for a complete, effective, and proper adjudication of the matter/issue involved in this case, i.e., the relaxation of the provisions of the PMR 2021 to consider it a proper party. 14. Even in its application, IEX has not made out any case as to how it is a necessary party or, at least, a proper party to the proceedings. All that has been submitted is that the Petitioner, under the guise of Power to Relax, is seeking permission to act contrary to the provision of the PMR 2021, and that too without impleading the other exchanges and affording an opportunity of hearing and representation, particularly when at the stage of the authorisation specific undertaking was given by the Petitioner pursuant to the specific objections being raised. It is also submitted that IEX has complied with the relevant regulation by having one of its clients surrender its ‘client’ status on its platform within the required timelines under the PMR 2021, and it would be prejudiced if the present Petition is allowed by the Commission. However, these submissions do not in any manner justify IEX being a proper party to this Petition. Whether the Petitioner has made out any case for relaxation of the provisions of the PMR 2021 for grant of time to PTC for diluting its stake to meet the requirement/compliance under Regulation 15 of the PMR 2021 needs to be examined on its own merits. A competing exchange cannot claim an opportunity of a hearing or making representation, as a matter of right, on the ground of being a proper party to such proceedings. Also, the prejudice averred by IEX does not appear to be a prejudice against any direct or legal interest but merely a commercial interest. In view of the above, we find that IEX is neither a necessary nor a proper party to these proceedings and its application for impleadment is therefore liable to be rejected.
title: Petition under Regulations 54, 55 and 56 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021 for grant of time to one of the Promoter Shareholders for diluting its stake in the Petitioner Company to meet the requirement/ compliance under Regulation 15 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Power Market) Regulations, 2021.
